notes: Every `status: "available"` tool was verified against the route table and the api-doc page named in its `doc` field on 2026-08-24. Every `status: "gap"` tool does NOT exist and is specified in ../BACKEND-GAPS.md.

No tool takes a customerId, userId or access token. Identity is the messaging identity, carried in the envelope described in defaults.identity_envelope, and resolved server-side by the same ladder /login uses. This is the single most important invariant in the catalog: a caller-supplied identity on the bot surface is account takeover.

`tier: "flow_only"` tools are NOT registered with the model. They are called by deterministic flow steps. Every money movement, every destructive action and every credential-adjacent read is in that tier.

geo-tracker is not reachable from this catalog. Live GPS is a WebSocket with a per-viewer access token, which the bot surface deliberately never holds; shipment progress in chat comes from orders_list_shipments instead.

jovi-mall.description: The commerce platform. Owns users, catalogue, cart, orders, shipments, money, tickets and the bot bridge. Default http://localhost:8022.

public.description: Unauthenticated jovi-mall routes under /api/public, plus the three payment routes that take no credential by design. Readable by anyone; nothing owner-scoped is reachable.

payment_public.description: POST /payments/initiate, /verify and /:id/authorize take NO authentication, deliberately — a payment link is shareable, so a mother may order and a son may pay. Withdrawn as an audit finding; do not 'fix' it. This is what makes in-chat mobile-money checkout possible without the bot ever holding a session.

webhook_command.description: The existing bot bridge: POST /api/webhooks/{whatsapp,telegram}. Dispatches a CommandBus command and returns the handler result verbatim — NOT the {success,data} envelope. The reply is in `message` and the automation layer relays it to the chat; this service sends nothing itself.

authentication.notes: BOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Mismatch or absence is 401 WEBHOOK_SECRET_INVALID. Unset is refused in production and open in development — see GAP-011, which argues that second half must change once registration lands.

bot_internal.description: BUILT 2026-08-25. A curated, service-token-authenticated surface at /api/internal/bot/*, carrying the resolved messaging identity. The backend resolves the customer from it and executes one named operation. No customer bearer token is ever issued to the automation layer, so a compromised automation layer cannot mint or hold a customer session.

authentication.notes: Same INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN geo-tracker presents on /api/internal/agents and /api/internal/shipments. The webhook secret is required IN ADDITION, so a leaked service token alone does not open the customer surface.

identity_envelope.description: Sent as the `identity` object on every bot_internal call, and derived by the automation layer from the inbound webhook — never from anything the customer typed.

shape.externalId: wa_phone_id (bare digits, e.g. 237600123456) for WhatsApp; chat_id for Telegram

identity_envelope.resolution: Server-side, by the ladder in modules/messaging-login/services/identity-resolver.service.ts: (1) channel_connections lookup; (2) WhatsApp only — the sender id IS the phone, repaired to E.164 by messagingPhoneToE164; (3) Telegram only — a chat_id matches no column, so an unbound chat is `needs_contact` and no customer-scoped tool may run.
identity_envelope.warning: wa_phone_id arrives from Meta as BARE DIGITS while login_phone is stored as strict E.164. A naive lookup matches nothing, for every user, while looking perfectly implemented.

response_envelope.error: { success: false, requestId: 'req_...', error: { code, message, statusCode, category, details? } }
response_envelope.rule: Branch on error.code; fall back to error.category, which is always present and is one of nine values. On `internal` and `external_service` the message is replaced with a generic sentence and details is omitted in every environment — requestId is the only handle.
response_envelope.exceptions: The bot webhook and the three payment routes do not use this envelope. Their `source` is `body`.

pagination.note: Ticket lists call the block `pagination`, not `meta`. Read both keys on the ticket tools.

tools.name: identity_resolve_sender
tools.title: Who is this sender?
tools.description: Find out whether the person messaging is a known customer, and get the handful of facts every later answer depends on: their display name, their language, and whether they can be served at all. Call this once at the start of a conversation and cache the result.
tools.when_to_use: As the first call of any conversation whose context is cold, and after any tool returns BOT_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not on every message — cache it for the conversation. Never to check whether an account exists for a number the customer typed; it only ever describes the sender.

parameters.description: No model-supplied parameters. The identity envelope is attached by the transport.

errors.when: No account for this messaging identity
Telegram, first contact — the chat is anonymous
The account is a vendor, agency or agent and holds no customer role

platform_notes.telegram: state `needs_contact` means the request_contact keyboard must be shown before any customer-scoped tool can run. A customer role is never auto-provisioned onto a business account.
platform_notes.whatsapp: The sender id is the phone number, so this resolves on first contact without any extra step.

tools.name: identity_sync_sender
tools.title: Sync the sender, creating an account if there is none
tools.description: Resolve the person messaging and CREATE a customer account for them if none exists. Returns whether this was their first message, and what is still missing from their profile.
tools.when_to_use: On EVERY inbound message, before anything else. It is the only call that creates an account, and it is cheap and writes nothing for an established customer.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never to check whether an account exists for a number the customer typed - it only ever describes the sender. Use identity_resolve_sender when the flow must not create anything, and during a readonly maintenance window when this route is refused.

parameters.description: No model-supplied parameters. The identity envelope is attached by the transport, and carries the optional `language` hint (Telegram from.language_code) used to seed a new account.

errors.when: The account exists and is suspended or closed - never routed around by creating a second one
This messaging identity is bound to a different account

tools.idempotency: Keyed on the messaging identity: a second call finds the account the first created and answers isNew:false. Idempotency-Key is required, as on every mutating bot route.
side_effects: Creates a User with roles:[customer] and a Customer profile when none exists
Attaches a customer role and profile to an EXISTING business account (vendor/agency/agent) - owner decision 2026-08-26, reversing GAP-002 D-3
Binds channel_connections(channel, externalId) to the account
Mints a system-generated password disclosed to nobody, exactly as POST /auth/register does for a customer

platform_notes.telegram: A chat_id maps to no phone number, so an unbound chat answers 200 with registered:false and onboarding.next.step:phone. RELAY onboarding.next.prompt verbatim and attach a request_contact keyboard because onboarding.next.requestContact is true - the same marker /login already uses. This is NOT an error.
platform_notes.whatsapp: The sender id IS the phone number, so an account is created and fully bound in one turn. The phone onboarding step is already provided.

tools.name: identity_submit_onboarding
tools.title: Submit or skip one onboarding step
tools.description: Record the customer answer to one profile question - or their refusal of it, so it is never asked again. The phone step is what creates the account on Telegram.
tools.when_to_use: Whenever onboarding.next on the previous response names a step and the customer has answered it. Walk next in order.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never guess a step. Never send action:skip for a step whose skippable is false - read it from next.

step.description: Take this from onboarding.next.step on the previous response.

action.description: skip is refused on a required step (phone, name).

contact.description: step:phone, Telegram only. The contact object from a request_contact reply. userId is REQUIRED and must be the sender own id - a contact shared from an address book carries none and is refused.

email.description: step:email. Written to the profile only - never promoted to a login identifier.

address.description: step:address. Same shape as addresses_add: a candidateRef from geo_search_address, never coordinates.

errors.when: The shared contact is not the sender own - the guard the whole Telegram flow rests on
A step other than phone was sent for a sender with no account yet
action:provide with the step own field absent
The address candidate handle is unknown or stale - run geo_search_address again
The shared phone number belongs to an account other than the one this chat is bound to

tools.idempotency: Re-providing a step overwrites it with the same value and is harmless. The address step spends a single-use candidate handle, so a retry answers BOT_GEO_CANDIDATE_EXPIRED rather than saving twice.
side_effects: step:phone CREATES the account on Telegram, or attaches this chat to an existing one
step:name and step:email write the value onto the Customer profile
step:address saves a geocoded address; the first one saved is always the default

platform_notes.telegram: step:phone is the contact-share completion and is the ONLY step reachable before an account exists.
platform_notes.whatsapp: step:phone is never pending - the sender id IS the number, so onboarding starts at name.

tools.name: auth_send_login_link
tools.title: Send a passwordless sign-in link and code
tools.description: Send the customer a magic link to tap and an 8-character code to type. Both sign them in on the website, both last 10 minutes, and using one kills the other.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks to sign in on the website, or when a tool needs an account this sender has not connected yet.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to authorise anything in chat — the bot surface never uses this credential, and a customer does not need it to shop through the bot. Not for a vendor, agency or agent: they get auth_send_password_reset_link instead.

errors.when: A shared contact was not the sender's own

tools.idempotency: A second /login revokes the first pair, so one identity never holds more than one live credential. That IS the repeat-safety property.
side_effects: Mints a 10-minute single-use session credential
Revokes any previously issued pair for this identity
Binds the messaging channel to the account on success, so notifications start working with no separate /connect

platform_notes.whatsapp: Relay `message` verbatim with preview_url: false. The result carries NO code and NO token field — the credentials are inside `message` only, because a webhook response body is logged in more places than a chat message.
platform_notes.telegram: `requestContact: true` on an unknown chat means attach the 'Share my phone number' keyboard. Relay with disable_web_page_preview: true.

tools.name: auth_send_password_reset_link
tools.title: Send a password-reset link
tools.description: Send a link that lets the sender choose a new password on the website. It lasts 30 minutes, is single-use, and nothing changes until they set a new password.
tools.when_to_use: Whenever anyone asks about a forgotten or changed password — and it is the ONLY tool that serves vendors, agencies and agents, because a password belongs to the account rather than to a role.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never collect, verify, suggest or repeat a password in chat, and never confirm identity by asking the customer questions. This tool is the entire password surface.

errors.when: A shared contact was not the sender's own

side_effects: Mints a 30-minute single-use reset token
Redeeming it stamps password_changed_at, which revokes every other live session on that account

platform_notes.telegram: The command name is `reset_password` with an UNDERSCORE while the user types `/reset-password` with a hyphen — and Telegram's bot_command entity stops at the hyphen, so parse from the raw message text, never from the entity. Its contact share is posted as `login_contact` like /login's; the platform's pending intent decides which command the contact completes.

tools.name: auth_complete_contact_share
tools.title: Complete a Telegram command with a shared contact
tools.description: Finish whichever command the customer was answering, using the phone number Telegram verified for them at signup.
tools.when_to_use: Post this for ANY inbound Telegram contact object, whatever command preceded it. The platform recorded which command asked and answers accordingly.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never branch on which command was asked — the automation layer does not have that information and the platform does. Never call it on WhatsApp.

contact.description: The WHOLE contact object as Telegram sent it, including user_id. Forwarding a subset breaks the security of the entire flow.

errors.when: contact.user_id is missing or is not the sender's own — a user can share somebody else's card from their address book

side_effects: Binds the Telegram chat to the matched account
Mints whichever credential the pending intent selected

platform_notes.telegram: Without the user_id guard, forwarding a victim's contact is a one-message account takeover. Relay error.message on a 400 — its wording is written for a chat window and does not read as an accusation, because the ordinary way to hit it is tapping the wrong contact.

tools.name: connections_send_connect_code
tools.title: Send a 6-character code to connect this chat to an account
tools.description: Give the sender a 6-character code they type on the website to connect this messaging account to their platform account, so notifications reach them here.
tools.when_to_use: When someone already signed in on the website wants their notifications delivered to this chat.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for signing in — that is auth_send_login_link. A customer who signs in through the bot has connected the channel by doing so and needs no code.
tools.idempotency: A second /connect invalidates the first code; one identity holds at most one live code.
side_effects: Mints a 10-minute single-use connection code. No account link is created here — the binding happens when the code is redeemed at POST /api/me/connections, where a session says who is claiming it.

tools.name: catalog_search_products
tools.title: Search and browse products
tools.description: Find products on sale, by words, category, price range, type or store. Returns a page of product cards with price, stock, rating and the store that sells them.
tools.when_to_use: Any time the customer describes something they want to buy, asks what is available, or narrows a previous search.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to look up a product code printed on a package — `q` is a whole-word text search over title, tags and description and does not match SKUs. Use catalog_resolve_sku. Not to fetch one known product: catalog_get_product returns far more.

q.description: Whole-word text search. Searching 'dres' will NOT find 'dress' — pass the customer's words, not a prefix.

category.description: Exact match. Get valid values from catalog_list_categories; do not invent one.

inStock.description: Only 'true' narrows. There is no way to ask for out-of-stock items.

sort.description: There is no popularity sort and asking for one is a 400, not a silent fallback.

errors.when: minPrice above maxPrice, an unknown sort, or a malformed filter

platform_notes.whatsapp: Render at most 10 rows as an interactive list; row title is capped at 24 characters and the description at 72, so the title must be truncated rather than the price dropped.
platform_notes.telegram: Photo cards with inline keyboards, or a numbered text list with a 'More' button.

tools.name: catalog_get_product
tools.title: Get one product in full
tools.description: Everything about one product: description, images, options, every variant with its own price and stock, the store, and the store's return and cancellation policies.
tools.when_to_use: Before answering any question about a specific product, and always before adding one to a cart — the variant id you need comes from here.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for browsing; the list rows from catalog_search_products are enough to choose from.

productId.description: The 24-character product id. Never a SKU and never a slug.

errors.when: Absent, draft, archived, suspended, or its vendor is suspended — indistinguishable on purpose

context_resolution.subject: product
context_resolution.notes: May be resolved from the product currently in focus. Echo the title, so the customer sees which product was understood.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A service variant's price is a UNIT RATE per durationMinutes, not the price — quote priceFrom with priceUnit or the customer is misquoted.
platform_notes.telegram: Select a variant on optionValueIds, never on a rebuilt option signature: renaming an option value is a supported operation that leaves the stored signature saying the old name.

tools.name: catalog_get_product_by_slug
tools.title: Get a product from a storefront link
tools.description: The same product detail, addressed the way a shared storefront link addresses it.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer pastes a storefront product URL. Product slugs are unique per vendor, not globally, so both halves are required.
tools.when_not_to_use: When you hold a product id — catalog_get_product returns an identical body with one parameter.

tools.name: catalog_resolve_sku
tools.title: Find the product a SKU belongs to
tools.description: Turn a product code printed on a package, a label or an advertisement into the product and variant it identifies.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer types something that looks like a product code rather than words.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for a search phrase — catalog_search_products handles words.

sku.description: The code as the customer typed it. Case is forgiven both ways (as-typed, upper and lower are all tried, and the as-typed spelling wins), EXCEPT for a SKU stored in mixed case, which resolves only when typed exactly. Send it unchanged — do not upper-case it first, or the as-typed rule works against you.

response.notes: The price and stock are the VARIANT's, not the product card's — a SKU usually names a variant that is not the default one a card quotes. `sku` comes back as STORED, which can differ in case from what was sent. Follow with catalog_get_product on `productId` when the customer wants the full card.

errors.when: Unknown SKU, or its product is not public

tools.name: catalog_list_categories
tools.title: List product categories
tools.description: The categories that currently have something for sale in them, with a count each.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks what is sold here, or before filtering a search by category — the values are free text and must come from this list.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not as a substitute for search when the customer already described what they want.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A complete small set, not a page — but still cap the rendered list at 10 rows and offer the rest as a second page.

tools.name: catalog_list_related_products
tools.title: Products often bought with this one
tools.description: Up to eight products related to this one, and — importantly — which kind of relation it is.
tools.when_to_use: After showing a product card, when the customer asks for alternatives or similar items.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never describe the result as 'customers also bought' unless meta.source is co_purchase. On a young catalogue the fallback is the common case and saying otherwise is a false claim about other shoppers.

platform_notes.whatsapp: meta.source is part of the contract. co_purchase -> 'Frequently bought together'; same_category -> 'More in this category'. `orders` is always null on the fallback. An empty list is a successful answer.

tools.name: catalog_get_store
tools.title: Get a store's public profile
tools.description: A seller's public page: name, description, city, whether they are verified, whether they are currently open, and the support contacts they chose to publish.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks who is selling something, or asks how to contact a seller — this is the source for the vendor branch of the support flow.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for the delivery company's contacts; those come from orders_list_shipments, because an agency is attached to a shipment rather than to a product.

errors.when: Unknown slug, or the vendor is suspended

platform_notes.whatsapp: Any support field may be null. A closed store (isOpen:false) still sells — say 'the seller is on holiday', never 'unavailable'.

tools.name: catalog_list_store_products
tools.title: List one store's products
tools.description: What a particular seller currently has for sale.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer wants to see more from a seller they have already seen.
tools.when_not_to_use: Use catalog_search_products with storeSlug when you also need to filter or sort within that store — the contract is identical and one call does both.

tools.name: catalog_list_product_reviews
tools.title: Read a product's reviews
tools.description: What buyers said about a product, and the star breakdown.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks whether a product is any good, or asks for opinions.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for delivery reviews — those are internal, feed an agent's trust score and have no public endpoint.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A product nobody has reviewed carries rating: null on the product card — never report that as zero stars.

tools.name: cart_get
tools.title: Show the cart
tools.description: What is currently in the customer's basket, line by line, with quantities and prices.
tools.when_to_use: Whenever the customer asks about their cart, and at the start of any checkout flow.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for the total payable — that is cart_quote, which adds delivery and validates the address.

platform_notes.whatsapp: An empty cart is a successful answer with items: [] and no cartId, never an error.

tools.name: cart_add_item
tools.title: Add an item to the cart
tools.description: Put a product variant in the customer's basket. If that exact variant is already there, its quantity goes up.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks to add something, and you already hold the variant id from catalog_get_product.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never guess a variant id, and never add a product that has more than one variant without asking which one. Never for a service product — services are booked, not carted, and the call is refused.

variantId.description: The sellable unit. Must belong to productId.

quantity.description: This ADDS to any quantity already on the line. To set an exact number use cart_set_item_quantity.

errors.when: The cart already holds the other product type
A digital product is already in the cart
The variant does not belong to the product

tools.idempotency: NOT idempotent — a repeat increments. The Idempotency-Key header (GAP-001) is what makes a chat retry safe; without it a delivery retry silently doubles the line.
side_effects: Adds or increments a cart line. Reserves no stock — stock is only held at checkout.

context_resolution.subject: product_variant
context_resolution.notes: May take the product from focus when exactly one product is in focus AND it has exactly one variant. A multi-variant product always requires an explicit choice. Echo the product title and variant name in the reply so the customer sees what was added.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A cart may hold items from several vendors but only ONE product type, and never a service.

tools.name: cart_set_item_quantity
tools.title: Set an exact quantity on a cart line
tools.description: Change a basket line to exactly this many.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer names a number they want — 'make it three'.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to remove a line: zero is refused. Use cart_remove_item.

errors.when: That variant is not in the cart

tools.idempotency: Naturally idempotent — it sets an absolute value.
side_effects: Does NOT refresh the line's snapshot price. The price is re-resolved at checkout, which is the moment that binds.

tools.name: cart_remove_item
tools.title: Remove one line from the cart
tools.description: Take one variant out of the basket.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks to remove a specific item.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to empty the whole basket — that is cart_clear and it needs confirmation.
side_effects: Removes exactly one variant. The by-product delete that removes every size of a garment is deliberately NOT exposed to the bot.

tools.name: cart_clear
tools.title: Empty the cart
tools.description: Remove everything from the basket.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the clear-cart flow, after the customer confirmed and was told how many items will go.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never as a way out of CART_MIXED_PRODUCT_TYPES without asking — the existing basket is something the customer chose.
side_effects: Discards every line. Nothing recovers it.

tools.name: cart_quote
tools.title: Price the cart before checking out
tools.description: What the basket will cost, and — when an address is named — whether that address can actually be delivered to.
tools.when_to_use: As the step of the checkout flow that runs BEFORE anything is created, with the chosen address id. It is the only cheap way to discover an unusable address.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for a running total while the customer shops; cart_get carries line prices.

deliveryAddressId.description: Optional, but always send it when one is chosen — it is validated by the same rule checkout applies.

errors.when: That address is not this customer's
The chosen address has no geocoded location — typed by hand rather than picked from address search

platform_notes.whatsapp: `delivery` is 0 and `total` equals the subtotal, and that is the truth rather than a stub: the agency's fee is charged to the vendor. Quote `absorbedByVendor` as 'delivery included' — never add it to the customer's total.

tools.name: checkout_create_orders
tools.title: Turn the cart into orders
tools.description: Create the customer's orders from their basket — one order per seller — and hold the stock for thirty minutes.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the checkout flow, after cart_quote succeeded with the chosen address and the customer confirmed the total, the address and the payment method.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never from the model, never speculatively, and never without a confirmation that named the total. It is the point at which stock is taken from other shoppers.

deliveryAddressId.description: Must be geocoded. Required explicitly here even though the API would fall back to the default, so the confirmation and the order cannot disagree about where it is going.

errors.when: A delivery agency on the order does not handle cash on delivery
Cash on delivery on a digital basket
A physical product has no resolvable delivery agency
Mixed currency, a service product, or a missing variant

tools.idempotency: NOT idempotent, and this is the highest-consequence gap in the catalog: a retried call creates a second set of orders and a second stock hold. Idempotency-Key (GAP-001) is mandatory on this route. Order creation is atomic across vendors — if any order fails, none are persisted and the cart is left intact.
side_effects: Creates one order per vendor, all sharing a cartId
Holds every line's stock for 30 minutes
Clears the cart
A cash-on-delivery checkout needs no payment call at all

platform_notes.whatsapp: The 30-minute stock hold is the flow's deadline. If payment is not started within it, tell the customer the hold lapsed rather than letting them discover it at the pay step.

tools.name: payment_initiate
tools.title: Start a mobile-money or card payment
tools.description: Charge the customer for a whole checkout group in one payment. On mobile money this produces either a code to dial or a request for an SMS code.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the payment flow, immediately after checkout_create_orders, with the cartId it returned and a phone number the customer just confirmed.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never on a cash-on-delivery checkout — no online payment exists for one. Never with a phone number taken from context; a payment phone number must be confirmed in the turn that spends it.

cartId.description: The checkout group. One payment settles every order in it.

phoneNumber.description: Strict E.164 with a leading +. Required unless the gateway is STRIPE.

phoneOperator.description: ASK the customer. Guessing wrong reaches them as 'payment declined'.

errors.when: The operator was not sent and cannot be derived from the number
The checkout is cash on delivery

tools.idempotency: Idempotent by reference — repeated calls with the same cartId return the existing transaction rather than charging twice.
side_effects: Creates or returns a PaymentTransaction
Sends a prompt to the customer's handset on the mobile-money path

context_resolution.subject: checkout_group
context_resolution.notes: The cartId must come from the checkout_create_orders result in this same flow. Never from a remembered value.

platform_notes.whatsapp: BRANCH ON status, NOT on the HTTP code. A gateway that refuses the charge answers HTTP 200 carrying status: FAILED — a client that reads only the HTTP status says 'waiting for your payment' forever. Branch on `instructions`: ussdCode means dial-and-approve; requiresOtp means collect an SMS code and there is NO ussdCode; clientSecret means Stripe and the flow must hand off to the web.

tools.name: payment_authorize_otp
tools.title: Submit the one-time code for a payment
tools.description: Pass on the code the customer received by SMS so their payment can go through.
tools.when_to_use: Only when payment_initiate returned instructions.requiresOtp — the My-CoolPay Orange Money path. Nothing happens until the code is relayed.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never on a payment that returned a USSD code; there is no SMS code coming and asking for one strands the customer.
side_effects: Authorises a live charge against the customer's mobile-money account

platform_notes.whatsapp: Never store the code in the conversation transcript. It is a live payment credential.

tools.name: payment_verify
tools.title: Check whether a payment has landed
tools.description: Ask the payment provider for the current state of a payment and apply it.
tools.when_to_use: From the payment flow's bounded poll after the customer says they approved the prompt.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not in a tight loop and not indefinitely. Webhooks settle the payment regardless — polling only makes the answer arrive sooner.
tools.idempotency: Settlement is idempotent; safe to call repeatedly.
side_effects: May settle the payment and fan out to every order in the group

tools.name: payment_get_transaction
tools.title: Read a payment the customer made
tools.description: The stored details of one of the customer's own payments.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks what happened to a specific payment.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not during a checkout poll — payment_verify is the live answer. Not on the public payment surface: reading a transaction requires ownership and the bot surface supplies it.

errors.when: Unknown id, malformed id, or not the customer's — indistinguishable on purpose

tools.name: orders_list_groups
tools.title: List the customer's orders
tools.description: The customer's order history, newest first, grouped the way they placed them — one group per checkout, however many sellers were in it.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about their orders in general, and as the first step of anything that needs an order the customer has not named.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to answer 'where is my parcel' — that needs orders_list_shipments, which carries the delivery status.

q.description: Substring over the order number and the line titles.

errors.when: An unknown status value — a 400 naming the field, never a silent empty page

platform_notes.whatsapp: The group paymentStatus is an aggregate: paid, awaiting_payment, partially_paid (including a cash order partway through per-shipment collection), refunded, failed, disputed, unknown, or mixed.

tools.name: orders_get_group
tools.title: Open one checkout group
tools.description: Everything the customer bought in one checkout, across every seller, with line items — and, for cash orders, the collection each shipment is waiting on.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer wants the detail of one purchase and it spanned several sellers.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for a single seller's order when you hold its id — orders_get_order is narrower.

errors.when: No orders for this cartId under this customer

platform_notes.whatsapp: codCollections[].deliveryCode is present on this response and MUST be stripped before the result reaches the model. It is the customer's proof-of-payment lever and is only ever disclosed by orders_get_cod_code, on explicit request, with its warning.

tools.name: orders_get_order
tools.title: Open one order
tools.description: One seller's order in full: what was bought, what it cost, where it is going, and how each line is being delivered.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer names an order number, or follows up on one order from a list.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to answer a delivery question on its own — pair it with orders_list_shipments.

orderId.description: The order id, or the order number the customer quoted — the bot surface accepts either.

errors.when: No such order, or it is somebody else's — indistinguishable on purpose

context_resolution.subject: order
context_resolution.notes: 'my order' with exactly one open order resolves to it, named in the reply. With more than one, disambiguate.

platform_notes.whatsapp: cartId is what makes an unpaid order resumable — payment_initiate takes the group, not the order.

tools.name: orders_list_shipments
tools.title: Where the customer's parcels are
tools.description: Each parcel on an order: its current stage, the history of how it got there, the delivery company and their support contacts, and — while it is actually moving — the first name of the person carrying it.
tools.when_to_use: This is the answer to 'where is my order'. Use it for every tracking, delivery-timing or delivery-problem question, and as the source for the delivery-company branch of the support flow.
tools.when_not_to_use: There is no live map in chat. Live GPS is a WebSocket in a separate service that needs a per-viewer token the bot deliberately never holds — describe the stage, never a position.

errors.when: No such order, or not this customer's

platform_notes.whatsapp: The status vocabulary is five words — preparing, shipped, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed — and they are the same five the customer's notifications use. `agent` is null far more often than set and each null means something different: no agent bound yet at preparing, and revoked on settlement at delivered. Never publish an agent phone number or full name; a customer with a question contacts the AGENCY. estimatedDelivery is always null — nothing estimates a delivery date, so never invent one.

tools.name: orders_get_cod_code
tools.title: Show the cash-on-delivery code
tools.description: The customer's secret six-digit code for a cash-on-delivery parcel, and the exact amount to pay.
tools.when_to_use: Only when the customer explicitly asks for their delivery code, and only from the cash-on-delivery flow.
tools.when_not_to_use: NEVER proactively, never as part of an order summary, and never in an answer to a general question about an order. Releasing it early is equivalent to signing a receipt before the goods arrive.

shipmentId.description: Required when the order has more than one parcel.

errors.when: Not a cash order, not picked up yet, or already collected

side_effects: Discloses a payment credential into a chat window

context_resolution.subject: order
context_resolution.notes: Deliberately stricter than every other order tool. A code must never be disclosed against an order the customer did not name.

platform_notes.whatsapp: Always send it with the warning: give this code to the delivery agent only AFTER you have received your package and paid. The code exists only while the collection is pending. Never write it to the conversation transcript, for the same reason the login reply is never logged.

tools.name: orders_resend_cod_code
tools.title: Issue a new cash-on-delivery code
tools.description: Replace a lost or locked delivery code with a new one.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer says they lost the code, or the agent entered it wrongly too many times.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not as a first response to 'what is my code' — show the existing one first.

errors.when: Within 60 seconds of the last one

side_effects: Invalidates the previous code
Sends the new code over WhatsApp as well

tools.name: orders_confirm_shipment_delivery
tools.title: Confirm a parcel arrived
tools.description: Record that the customer received a parcel. Once every parcel on an order is confirmed, the order completes and the seller's money starts its hold.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the confirmation flow, after the customer confirmed they physically have the parcel.
tools.when_not_to_use: NEVER on a cash-on-delivery parcel — that is confirmed by handing the agent the code, and calling this is refused. Never on the customer's behalf because a status says the agent reported delivery: this is the customer's word, and it is the lever they hold in a dispute.

errors.when: Not yet reported delivered, OR the order is cash on delivery

tools.idempotency: A repeat answers SHIPMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED rather than doing it twice.
side_effects: Confirming the last parcel completes the order and starts the seller's 7-day escrow hold

tools.name: orders_cancel
tools.title: Cancel an order
tools.description: Call off an order that has not shipped and has not been paid.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the cancellation flow, after the customer confirmed against a summary naming the order number and total.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never on a paid order — that needs a refund and this endpoint performs none. Never when a parcel has left the depot: at that point the customer can still refuse it at the door, which is a different conversation.

reason.description: The customer's own words, not a paraphrase.

errors.when: Past preparing, or the payment state is not unpaid
The seller's cancellation policy refuses it

side_effects: Sets the order cancelled and its payment failed
Notifies the seller

context_resolution.subject: order
context_resolution.notes: Deliberately explicit_only. 'Cancel it' resolved from focus against the wrong order is unrecoverable.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A cash order additionally requires that no parcel has been picked up. Cancellation is gated by the SELLER's policy — quote their terms from the product card rather than promising an outcome.

tools.name: profile_get_summary
tools.title: The customer's profile, in brief
tools.description: The handful of profile facts that matter in a chat: display name, language, currency, whether contact details are verified, and how many addresses are saved.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks what the platform knows about them, or before a settings change.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to fetch an address to deliver to — addresses_list is narrower and returns the ids checkout needs.

platform_notes.whatsapp: The bot surface returns MASKED contact details. A chat window is a shared, screenshotted, sometimes-shoulder-surfed place, and the customer already knows their own number.

tools.name: profile_set_language
tools.title: Change the customer's language
tools.description: Set the language the platform writes to this customer in — in chat, in notifications and in email.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks to change language, or writes consistently in a language other than the one on their profile and confirms the switch.
tools.when_not_to_use: Do not switch on a single message in another language. People code-switch; a preference change is durable and reaches their email too.

language.description: The five languages the platform's copy is written in.

side_effects: Every later notification, in every channel, is written in this language

platform_notes.whatsapp: Product text is NOT translated — it is vendor-authored in one language and the product carries contentLanguage saying which. Say so rather than appearing to have translated it.

tools.name: addresses_list
tools.title: List saved delivery addresses
tools.description: The customer's saved addresses, which is the default, and — crucially — whether each one can actually be delivered to.
tools.when_to_use: As the address step of checkout, and whenever the customer asks where their orders go.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to find a new address — that is geo_search_address.

platform_notes.whatsapp: `deliverable` is the bot surface's rendering of 'has a geocoded location'. An address without one is refused at checkout, so an undeliverable address must be shown as needing to be re-picked rather than offered as a choice.

tools.name: addresses_add
tools.title: Save a delivery address
tools.description: Save an address the customer picked from address search or shared as a location, so it can be delivered to.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the address flow, and only with a candidate that came from geo_search_address or geo_reverse_address in this same flow.
tools.when_not_to_use: NEVER from text the customer typed. An address without a geocoded location is refused at checkout, and saving one produces an address that looks fine and cannot be used.

label.description: What the customer calls it — Home, Work.

geoCandidateRef.description: An opaque handle to a candidate returned by geo_search_address or geo_reverse_address within this flow. The coordinates are never re-sent by the caller.

addressLine2.description: Flat number, landmark, directions — the part a geocoder never knows.

errors.when: The candidate handle is unknown or older than the flow window

tools.idempotency: The candidate handle is single-use, which stops a retry saving the address twice.
side_effects: Adds a saved address
isDefault: true clears the flag on every other address

platform_notes.whatsapp: A null location inside the indexed address array makes the whole customer document unwritable — the key must be omitted, never sent as null. That is why this tool takes a candidate handle instead of raw coordinates: the backend never receives a null to write.
platform_notes.telegram: Accept a shared location as the input to geo_reverse_address, then confirm the formatted address before saving. A pin is not an address.

tools.name: addresses_set_default
tools.title: Make an address the default
tools.description: Choose which saved address new orders go to unless another is picked.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks to change where their orders go by default.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not as part of checkout — checkout takes the address explicitly, so changing the default there changes a durable setting the customer did not ask about.
side_effects: Clears the default flag on every other address

tools.name: geo_search_address
tools.title: Turn typed text into real addresses
tools.description: Turn what the customer typed into a short list of real, mappable addresses for them to choose from.
tools.when_to_use: The first step of the address flow whenever the customer describes where they live in words.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never skip the customer's choice. The point of this step is that a human confirms which candidate is right; picking the first result for them is how an order is delivered to the wrong street.
side_effects: Mints a short-lived single-use candidateRef for each result, which addresses_add consumes

platform_notes.whatsapp: Render candidates as an interactive list, capped at 10 rows, and never more than five — a chat window is a bad place to scan a long list of similar streets.

tools.name: geo_reverse_address
tools.title: Turn a shared location into an address
tools.description: Turn a pin the customer shared into the address it sits on.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer shares their location. Both platforms support it and it is the fastest, most accurate path to a deliverable address.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never save the result without showing the customer the address it resolved to and having them confirm. A pin dropped indoors resolves to a neighbouring building often enough to matter.
side_effects: Mints a single-use candidateRef

platform_notes.whatsapp: The result may be null when nothing matches — say so and fall back to geo_search_address rather than inventing a street.
platform_notes.telegram: Ask with a request_location keyboard button rather than in prose.

tools.name: support_resolve_contacts
tools.title: Work out who the customer should be talking to
tools.description: For the thing the customer most recently dealt with, who to contact: the seller, the delivery company, or the platform — with each one's published contacts and why it is relevant.
tools.when_to_use: For any 'I need help' that is not obviously about one specific thing, and as the first step of the support flow. A product question goes to the seller; a parcel question goes to the delivery company; a money or account question goes to the platform.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for a question you can answer from the catalogue or the customer's own orders. Routing someone to a phone number is a worse answer than telling them where their parcel is.

scope.description: auto walks the relevance ladder. The others answer for one party only, and say so when there is no such party in context.

hintProductId.description: The product currently in focus in the conversation, if any. A product id (24 hex characters) — a slug is unique per vendor, not globally, so it cannot be resolved here. Overrides the server's own recency signal, and an id the customer cannot see is a 404 rather than a fall-through.

hintOrderId.description: The order currently in focus, if any. An order id OR the order number the customer read out (as orders_get_order accepts). Wins over hintProductId when both are sent, and an order that is not theirs is a 404 rather than a fall-through.

errors.when: Nothing recent to route from, on a NAMED party scope. scope:auto never raises it — with no context it answers 200 with the platform alone
The named scope has no party — most often agency, which only exists once an order has shipped

context_resolution.subject: recent_interaction
context_resolution.notes: Always name what it routed from — 'about your order ORD-2026-000123 from Maison Bella'. A support contact for the wrong purchase is worse than asking.

platform_notes.whatsapp: An agency has no contacts until an order has a shipment, so /support:agency on a product-only context legitimately has nothing to answer with. Any contact field may be null; offer the ones that exist and fall through to a ticket.

tools.name: tickets_list
tools.title: List the customer's support tickets
tools.description: The support tickets this customer has open, and their current status.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about a support request they already made, or before opening a new one — an existing open ticket about the same thing should be added to rather than duplicated.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not as the answer to a first-time question. Most questions are answered better than by opening a ticket.

status.description: Authoritative values are in agency/tickets.md. Omit to get open tickets.

platform_notes.whatsapp: The pagination block on ticket lists is called `pagination`, not `meta`. assigned_admin is null until a human takes the ticket, which is the state almost every ticket is in — say 'waiting to be picked up', never invent a handler.

tools.name: tickets_get
tools.title: Read one ticket
tools.description: One support ticket with its public conversation.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer names a ticket number or asks what happened to a request.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for a list — tickets_list is cheaper and paginated.

ticketId.description: The ticket id or the TKT- number the customer quoted.

platform_notes.whatsapp: Customers never see internal staff notes; only public ones are returned. Do not imply there is a hidden conversation.

tools.name: tickets_create
tools.title: Open a support ticket
tools.description: Raise a support request with the platform, optionally attached to the order or product it is about.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the support flow, once the question could not be answered and the customer confirmed a summary of what will be sent.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not before trying to answer. Not when an open ticket already covers it — add a note instead.

description.description: The customer's own account of the problem. Summarise the conversation faithfully; do not add conclusions they did not reach.

type.description: Valid values are in ticket_types.txt. order_issue is the common one.

errors.when: A field fails the schema, or an unknown type

tools.idempotency: Not idempotent — a retry opens a second ticket. The confirmation token being single-use is the practical guard; Idempotency-Key (GAP-001) is the real one.
side_effects: Creates a ticket visible to platform staff
Notifies the support queue

tools.name: tickets_add_note
tools.title: Reply on a ticket
tools.description: Add the customer's message to an existing ticket.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer says something more about a ticket that is already open.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to record your own summary. A note is attributed to the customer and read by staff as their words.
side_effects: Adds a PUBLIC note. Customers cannot create internal notes and the attempt is refused server-side.

tools.name: tickets_close
tools.title: Close a ticket
tools.description: Mark a support request as resolved.
tools.when_to_use: Only when the customer explicitly says the matter is settled and confirms.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never because a conversation went quiet, and never to tidy up. Only the customer decides their problem is over.

tools.name: wishlist_list
tools.title: The customer's saved products
tools.description: Products the customer saved for later, newest save first.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks what they saved, or wants to buy something they saved earlier.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not as a browse surface — it is their own short list, not the catalogue.

platform_notes.whatsapp: An entry's `product` can be null when the product went off sale. Say 'no longer available' and offer to remove it — never drop the row silently, and never say why it went, which would leak a seller's catalogue state.

tools.name: wishlist_add
tools.title: Save a product for later
tools.description: Add a product to the customer's saved list.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer likes something but is not buying it now.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not instead of adding to the cart when they said they want to buy it.

errors.when: Not on sale, or does not exist

tools.idempotency: Idempotent by design — saving something already saved answers 200 and does not move the entry, because a wishlist is ordered by when you decided.

tools.name: wishlist_remove
tools.title: Remove a saved product
tools.description: Take a product off the customer's saved list.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer says they are no longer interested, or clears an unavailable entry.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not after adding it to the cart. Those are different lists and the customer did not ask.

tools.name: recently_viewed_record
tools.title: Record that a product was shown
tools.description: Note that the customer opened a product, so the platform's idea of what they were last looking at stays current.
tools.when_to_use: Automatically, by the flow step that renders a product card. It is what keeps the support routing and the website's recently-viewed list in agreement with the conversation.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never from the model, never for a product merely mentioned in a search result, and never for one the customer did not open.
tools.idempotency: Re-viewing moves the entry to the head rather than duplicating it; there is never a duplicate.
side_effects: Moves the entry to the head of a capped list, evicting the oldest
Updates recentProductCode on the profile, which the support routing reads

platform_notes.whatsapp: There is deliberately no client-supplied timestamp and sending one is a 400 — the server clock is the only source, because the list is ordered and capped by it.

tools.name: digital_list_entitlements
tools.title: The customer's digital purchases
tools.description: Everything the customer bought as a download, and whether each one can still be downloaded.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about a file they bought.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for physical orders.

platform_notes.whatsapp: maxDownloads null means unlimited and expiresAt null means never expires — say so in words rather than printing null. canDownload is the single flag that decides whether to offer the download.

tools.name: digital_create_download_link
tools.title: Send a download link
tools.description: Give the customer a link to download a file they bought. It works once and lasts fifteen minutes.
tools.when_to_use: From the downloads flow, when the customer asks for a specific file and canDownload is true.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not speculatively and not for several files at once. Each executed download counts against the customer's allowance.
tools.idempotency: Minting a link costs nothing; the allowance moves on EXECUTE, not on creation, so an unused link is free.
side_effects: Mints a single-use 15-minute token that carries its own authority — anyone holding the URL can download the file

platform_notes.whatsapp: The url is relative — prefix it with the API base. Send it with preview_url: false; it is a bearer credential in a URL.

tools.name: bookings_list
tools.title: The customer's appointments
tools.description: Appointments the customer has booked, with when they are and whether they are confirmed and paid.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about an appointment or a service they booked.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to make a booking — booking needs a slot lock against a live calendar and is handed off to the website.

platform_notes.whatsapp: Times are formatted in the customer's own timezone. The pagination block here uses totalPages, not pages.

tools.name: bookings_get
tools.title: One appointment in detail
tools.description: One appointment, including anything still owed after it was settled.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about a specific appointment, or about a balance they were told about.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to list — bookings_list is cheaper.

platform_notes.whatsapp: creditDue is RECORDED, not refunded — if the provider settled below what was paid, say the provider intends to hand it back and offer support, never promise a refund.

tools.name: bookings_cancel
tools.title: Cancel an appointment
tools.description: Call off an appointment, subject to the provider's cancellation policy.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the cancellation flow, after the customer confirmed against a summary naming the service and the time.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never for a rescheduling request. Moving an appointment needs a new slot locked first, and cancelling instead loses the original slot.
side_effects: Releases the slot
A paid booking is refunded where the gateway supports it; on My-CoolPay and cash bookings the payment status becomes refund_pending and a support ticket is raised for a manual payout

platform_notes.whatsapp: Do not promise an automatic refund. Say the cancellation succeeded and report the payment status the response actually carries.

tools.name: reviews_check_eligibility
tools.title: May the customer review this?
tools.description: Whether the customer is allowed to review a product or a delivery — and if not, why.
tools.when_to_use: Before offering to take a review, so an ineligible customer is never asked for one.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not after a failed submission — this is the check that avoids one.

subjectType.description: delivery takes a SHIPMENT id, not an order id.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A 200 with eligible:false is a successful answer to a question, not a failure. reason is the same code the write path would have raised.

tools.name: reviews_create
tools.title: Leave a review
tools.description: Record the customer's rating, and their words if they gave any, about a product they bought or a delivery they received.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the review flow, after eligibility was checked and the customer confirmed what will be published.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never write prose on the customer's behalf, never infer a rating from their tone, and never review a delivery against an order id — the subject is a shipment.

body.description: The customer's own words, verbatim. Optional.

errors.when: Not completed, not delivered, or a delivered shipment with no agent bound

side_effects: A bare star rating PUBLISHES IMMEDIATELY and moves the product's public rating
A review carrying prose is held for a human moderator
A delivery review is internal, is attributed to the carrying agent server-side, and feeds their trust score

platform_notes.whatsapp: Tell the customer which of the two happens: a rating alone goes live at once, prose waits for a moderator. A delivery review is never published anywhere.

tools.name: notifications_get_preferences
tools.title: How the customer is contacted
tools.description: Which channel the customer gets notifications on and which kinds of update they have switched on.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about the messages they get, or complains about too many or too few.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to explain a single notification they received — answer the underlying question instead.

platform_notes.whatsapp: At most ONE secondary channel is on at a time; enabling one disables the others. Money messages and cancellations always send and no setting silences them — say so plainly rather than implying everything is switchable.

tools.name: notifications_update_preferences
tools.title: Change how the customer is contacted
tools.description: Switch a kind of update on or off, or move notifications to a different channel.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the notification-settings flow, after confirming exactly what will change.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never in response to 'stop messaging me' alone. Money messages and cancellations cannot be switched off, so silently changing something else answers a request that was not granted.

channel.description: The single secondary channel. Setting one disables the other two.

errors.when: Enabling a channel that is not verified

side_effects: Changes where every future notification is delivered

tools.name: payment_create_pay_link
tools.title: Get a page the customer can pay by card on
tools.description: A short-lived link to a page where the customer completes a CARD payment. Mobile money never needs this — it finishes on the customer's handset.
tools.when_to_use: After payment_initiate with gateway STRIPE, when the customer chose to pay by card. Send them the url.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never for mobile money — that completes in the chat and this refuses it. Never for a payment that is already done. If url comes back null the deployment has no payment page: offer mobile money instead.

errors.when: Unknown id, malformed id, or not the customer's — indistinguishable on purpose
A mobile-money payment, which completes on the handset and needs no page
The payment is already settled, failed or cancelled

tools.notes: A second call REVOKES the first link. Ask for a new one only when the customer says the old one stopped working.

tools.name: messaging_get_window
tools.title: Can I still message this customer in my own words?
tools.description: Whether WhatsApp's 24-hour service window is still open for this customer, and when it closes. Telegram has no such window and always answers open.
tools.when_to_use: Before starting a flow that may finish after the customer stops writing — a payment they will approve later, an order that ships in two days. Decides whether the flow can end in the chat or must hand off to messaging_notify_customer.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not before an ordinary reply. Answering a message the customer just sent is always inside the window.
tools.notes: expiresAt is the platform's own 23-hour window, deliberately earlier than Meta's 24. Read it as 'after this we switch to a template', never as when Meta closes. applicable:false means the channel has no window at all (Telegram).

tools.name: messaging_notify_customer
tools.title: Ask the platform to message the customer for you
tools.description: Hands one situation to the platform to deliver, in the customer's language, through whichever channel reaches them — free-form inside the WhatsApp window, an approved template outside it.
tools.when_to_use: When you have something to tell the customer and cannot send it yourself: the service window has closed, or the flow is ending and the answer comes later. Today the only situation is order.payment_link — a card payment page.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never as a general send. It takes a named situation, never a message you wrote. There is no marketing situation and there will not be one.

situation.description: The closed set of situations the automation layer may raise. One member today.

transactionId.description: The card payment to send a page for. Must be the customer's own.

errors.when: Unknown id, malformed id, or not the customer's — indistinguishable on purpose
A mobile-money payment, or a deployment with no payment page configured
The payment is already settled, failed or cancelled

tools.notes: A 200 means accepted for delivery, not delivered — the platform never fails a business action over a notification. Do not tell the customer a message was sent. This mints a fresh pay link, so it REVOKES any earlier one.
